knowledge_point.title: Finding a Point on a Line That Is Closest to a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
![](closest-d51d093f969bfea80a0e8674.png)

Find the point on the line $4y+3x=5$ that is closest to the point $(-3,0)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The closest point is where the given line meets the perpendicular line through $(-3,0)$.

First, rewrite the given line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}4y+3x&=5 \\ 4y&=-3x+5 \\ y&=-\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

The given line has slope $-\frac{3}{4}$, so the perpendicular slope is $\frac{4}{3}$, its negative reciprocal. Using point-slope form,

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(0)&=\frac{4}{3}\left(x-(-3)\right) \\ y&=\frac{4}{3}x+4+(0) \\ y&=\frac{4}{3}x+4\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve the system

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y &=-\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{5}{4} \\ y &=\frac{4}{3}x+4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

by setting the expressions for $y$ equal and collecting terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{5}{4}&=\frac{4}{3}x+4 \\ \left(-\frac{3}{4}-\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)\right)x&=4-\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) \\ -\frac{25}{12}x&=\frac{11}{4} \\ x&=-\frac{33}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the given line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y&=-\frac{3}{4}\left(-\frac{33}{25}\right)+\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) \\ y&=\frac{99}{100}+\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) \\ y&=\frac{56}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point on the line $4y+3x=5$ closest to $(-3,0)$ is $(-\frac{33}{25},\frac{56}{25})$.

knowledge_point.title: Finding a Point on a Line That Is Closest to a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
![](closest-44a103edc904609f5f406f60.png)

Find the point on the line $4y-3x=2$ that is closest to the point $(4,-4)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The closest point is where the given line meets the perpendicular line through $(4,-4)$.

First, rewrite the given line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}4y-3x&=2 \\ 4y&=3x+2 \\ y&=\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The given line has slope $\frac{3}{4}$, so the perpendicular slope is $-\frac{4}{3}$, its negative reciprocal. Using point-slope form,

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(-4)&=-\frac{4}{3}\left(x-(4)\right) \\ y&=-\frac{4}{3}x+\frac{16}{3}+(-4) \\ y&=-\frac{4}{3}x+\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve the system

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y &=\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{1}{2} \\ y &=-\frac{4}{3}x+\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

by setting the expressions for $y$ equal and collecting terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{1}{2}&=-\frac{4}{3}x+\frac{4}{3} \\ \left(\frac{3}{4}-\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)\right)x&=\frac{4}{3}-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\ \frac{25}{12}x&=\frac{5}{6} \\ x&=\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the given line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y&=\frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\ y&=\frac{3}{10}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\ y&=\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point on the line $4y-3x=2$ closest to $(4,-4)$ is $(\frac{2}{5},\frac{4}{5})$.

knowledge_point.title: Finding a Point on a Line That Is Closest to a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
![](closest-169e4ebfb9ddf19a685f8d89.png)

Find the point on the line $3y-2x=-5$ that is closest to the point $(-5,-2)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The closest point is where the given line meets the perpendicular line through $(-5,-2)$.

First, rewrite the given line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}3y-2x&=-5 \\ 3y&=2x-5 \\ y&=\frac{2}{3}x-\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The given line has slope $\frac{2}{3}$, so the perpendicular slope is $-\frac{3}{2}$, its negative reciprocal. Using point-slope form,

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(-2)&=-\frac{3}{2}\left(x-(-5)\right) \\ y&=-\frac{3}{2}x-\frac{15}{2}+(-2) \\ y&=-\frac{3}{2}x-\frac{19}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve the system

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y &=\frac{2}{3}x-\frac{5}{3} \\ y &=-\frac{3}{2}x-\frac{19}{2}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

by setting the expressions for $y$ equal and collecting terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}x-\frac{5}{3}&=-\frac{3}{2}x-\frac{19}{2} \\ \left(\frac{2}{3}-\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)\right)x&=-\frac{19}{2}-\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right) \\ \frac{13}{6}x&=-\frac{47}{6} \\ x&=-\frac{47}{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute into the given line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y&=\frac{2}{3}\left(-\frac{47}{13}\right)+\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right) \\ y&=-\frac{94}{39}+\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right) \\ y&=-\frac{53}{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point on the line $3y-2x=-5$ closest to $(-5,-2)$ is $(-\frac{47}{13},-\frac{53}{13})$.
